minutes.headline: Open Space committee approved May minutes and backed joint meetings with the planning board on future land first-refusal offers.
minutes.summary: The committee approved the May 10 minutes by roll call. It learned the select board had already declined the right of first refusal on the Leominster Road parcel. Discussion centered on how the short state first-refusal window strains review, with a proposal for joint meetings with the planning board, and on stalled title work for the Stump Cove and Palmetto Road lake-access parcels.

what_happened.line: The committee agreed to pursue joint meetings with the planning board whenever a state first-refusal notice arrives; a member will bring the idea to that board.
The select board had already declined the right of first refusal on the Leominster Road parcel, the committee learned.
A member said a pledged-funds interest in an apple orchard parcel went unpursued because the 120-day first-refusal window prevented action.
The Conservation Commission was awarded a state Mass Trails grant, pending federal approval, with a local match; consultant work will probably need multiple bids.
The chair will reopen the public lake access discussion once the Stump Cove title issue is resolved; no votes other than approving the May minutes were taken.

why_it_matters: When land comes up for sale, the short state first-refusal window limits how much review the town can give before it must decide whether to buy, so a joint committee process could change how quickly conservation land purchases reach residents' votes.
Public access to the lake depends on unresolved title work for two parcels, and a local match on the trail grant would be a town spending question if it reaches a budget.
